title: Ghost in the Machine: a preregistered, null-calibrated laboratory for authorship, emergence and specificity in synthetic self-models
description: Synthetic computational experiments on self-modelling recurrent agents. v4 re-adjudicates the v3 'cross-theory' event (a gain ramp measured against an early baseline and held on by detector hysteresis) and tests, with a cryptographically locked preregistration, cross-yoked twins, paired lesions, placebo contrasts, a calibrated four-rung null ladder and 48 held-out networks, whether authoring one's own actions stabilizes the collective dynamics of a self-model through an efference-copy/comparator loop. Nothing in this software creates, detects or measures consciousness. v5 adds six preregistered follow-up studies: the authorship-stabilization effect replicates, scales with authorship, survives nonlinear estimators and other architectures, is an online comparator effect and follows the comparator's wiring; the causal-emergence (Psi) component and hence the GHOST-v4 verdict did not replicate.
